title: Galois equivariant marked nodal alteration with birational quotients
statement:
Let $Y$ be an affine integral excellent Noetherian scheme, let $P$ be an integral excellent scheme, and let $f:P\to Y$ be proper dominant. Suppose its generic fibre is a smooth geometrically integral curve. Let $E\subset P$ be an effective Cartier divisor with finite etale generic fibre, possibly empty. There are a finite group $G$, integral excellent separated Noetherian schemes $C,Y'$, a commutative square $fa=bf'$ with $a:C\to P$ and $b:Y'\to Y$ projective alterations that are generically etale, and a $G$-equivariant projective flat finitely presented morphism $f':C\to Y'$. The group acts trivially on $P,Y$. There are a $G$-stable nowhere dense closed subset $T'\subset Y'$ and a $G$-stable effective Cartier divisor $D\subset C$ such that every geometric fibre of $f'$ is a nonempty connected curve with at worst ordinary double points, $f'$ is smooth off $T'$, $D\to Y'$ is finite etale, $D$ is in the smooth locus of $f'$, and $a^{-1}|E|\subseteq |D|\cup(f')^{-1}T'$. The action on $Y'\setminus T'$ is free. The actions on $C,Y'$ are admissible (every orbit is contained in an affine open); their finite scheme quotients $Q=C/G$ and $Y'/G$ exist and are integral excellent Noetherian. The morphisms $Q\to P$ and $Y'/G\to Y$ are proper birational. The generic fibre of $f'$ is smooth geometrically integral. An alteration means proper surjective and finite over a dense open; birational means an isomorphism on dense open subschemes; an ordinary double point has completed geometric-fibre ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. A scheme quotient has orbit-space topology and structure sheaf of invariant sections. Projectivity here is in the closed-immersion into projective-space convention; the affine base permits this form.

Conventions for the notions used here: [def-pc-scheme], [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

source.place: Expose IX Theorem 1.2 (all six clauses), printed pp. 131--132, and beginning of IX 1.4, p. 132 (admissibility, existence and excellence of quotients). The proper birational quotient conclusion is clause (iii). Finite etaleness of D follows from its properness and etaleness. The affine-base projectivity conversion is the same as in lem-trf-relative-marked-nodal-reduction.
